blocking_defects.failed_criterion: quality_contract contact_and_consequence ('objects have visible support and continuous identity') and continuity, plus the brief's rejection of unmotivated disappearance.
blocking_defects.defect: In A's menu-tap and pay-mark views, OrderPassFilm.tsx draws the tapping hand only while `S.s3.tapGo>0&&S.s3.tapBack<1` (and `payGo>0&&payBack<1`). tapBack is ease5((r3-.74)/.26), so it reaches exactly 1 when s3-event-3 ends at 15.54+3.51+1.2 = 20.25 s. At that frame the finger is resting at its `away` point, contact + (300,420)*fs. For menu-tap:a (phone at 520,760, scale 1.5, Chow mein contact at about 547,631, fs 1.3) that point is about (937,1177), on screen. The ease brings the hand to rest there, and the next frame removes it. The fingertip and finger shaft (about 200 px) and the left part of a hand drawn at 1.3x simply vanish about 1.05 s before the 21.30 s cut. The same construction repeats in pay-mark:a. Its away point is about (841,1345) with fs 1, and most of the on-screen hand vanishes at the s3-event-4 end, 15.54+5.955+1.2 = 22.695 s, about 0.85 s before the 23.55 s cut. The guest's order and pay actions, the only human ordering actions in the film, therefore end in a pop instead of the hand leaving frame. B's paid-close sends the hand to about (1239,1579), off frame, and B's menu-tap keeps the jointed arm drawn throughout, so this defect is A's alone. Correction, if A were ever repaired: carry the away point fully off frame, or keep the hand drawn through the cut.

strongest_frame: s4 printer-idle into paid-line, 23.55 to 25.813 s. The printer stands idle beside an empty, unlit wok (wokCold, flame 0, food 0). The paid mark travels its dashed line into a printer at scale 1.3. orderState puts the arrival at 24.603+0.97*0.945 = 25.52 s and the lamp's answer at 25.52 to 25.64 s, both inside this shot, about 0.29 s before the cut. This repairs the round-1 pacing defect in A's construction.
weakest_frame: s3 menu-tap and pay-mark details, 19.05 to 23.55 s. The tapping hand pops out of existence on screen at 20.25 s and again at 22.695 s (blocking defect above). Secondarily, the s4 ticket-print detail is 0.697 s long (25.813 to 26.51 s), and the ticket completes at about 26.36 s, leaving about a 0.15 s hold before the wok-flare wide.

A's archived phone-selection weaknesses (no visible walkout, small ledger in a dark desk frame, pen over rule text at about 45.2 to 45.8 s, thin s9 quote frame, final tag near the panel pole) were comparative reasons in the selection, not blocking defects. They are pixel matters I can't decide from code, and they stay in the archive unchanged.

Code scope only. No pixel, motion, legibility or finish observation is claimed, and this report approves no film.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: Intended chain from the code at counter level. The storefront door swings shut with its bell, the apron swings on the stand hook and the desk phone rings unanswered while two tables wait with empty plates. An empty sign frame hangs on the glass and the host panel lights and writes Haniya, then an AI host tag hooks on. A hand lifts the phone over the table code, the brackets lock and the menu opens. A fingertip taps Chow mein and then Pay, which becomes the paid mark. The mark travels into the idle printer, the lamp turns red and the ticket rises and hangs. Only then a cook pours noodles into the wok as the flame flares. The owner's $9,650 a month is stamped OWNER COUNT beside a bare clip. Coins arc into the jar at the pass under a FOX 26 tag. The rule card's cooks line lights and is circled, and the restaurant folder's box stays blank under a question mark. A hand raises the phone, hesitates and lowers it beside a customer quote card. The panel takes an order, a slip drops into the printer, and the jar ends under owner says and no record shown tags.
story_review.opening_to_ending: It opens on an unattended station that asks who takes the order. It ends with the panel taking the order and the jar under two tags, answering that software takes the order and the tip rests on the owner's word, without inventing an outcome.
story_review.weakest_transition: s8 to s9 (49.4 s). The cut goes from the blank tip-credit box in the folder to a hand hesitating at a table code, so the thread moves from the money limit to ordering friction with no carried object. The close then returns to the jar.
